'''Robert Graham Cooks''' is the Henry Bohn Hass Distinguished Professor of Chemistry in the Aston Laboratories for Mass Spectrometry at [[Purdue University]]. He is an ISI Highly Cited Chemist,{{R|HC}} with over 1,000 publications and an H-index of 150.{{R|web}}<ref>{{cite web | title=Robert Graham Cooks | website=Google Scholar | url=https://scholar.google.co.za/citations?hl=en&user=_Jxju_sAAAAJ | access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref>

==Education==
Cooks received Bachelor of Science and Master of Science degrees from the [[University of Natal]] in South Africa in 1961 and 1963, respectively. He received a Ph.D. from the University of Natal in 1965 and a second Ph.D. from [[Cambridge University]] in 1967, where he worked with [[Peter Sykes (chemist)|Peter Sykes]]. He then did post-doctoral work at Cambridge with [[Dudley Williams (biochemist)|Dudley Williams]].<ref name="NAS"/>

==Career==
Cooks became an assistant professor at [[Kansas State University]] from 1968 to 1971. In 1971, he  took a position at [[Purdue University]]. He became a professor of chemistry in 1980 and  was appointed the Henry Bohn Hass Distinguished Professor in 1990.<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=R. Graham Cooks |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/r-graham-cooks-ylu0hc/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>
Cooks was co-editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry]]'' from 2013 to 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Co-editors of the Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry - Volume 6, 2013 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?2013,anchem |website=Annual Reviews Directory |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Co-editors of the Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry - Volume 10, 2017 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?2017,anchem |website=Annual Reviews Directory |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>

== Select research interests==
Research in Cooks' laboratory (the Aston Laboratories) has contributed to a diverse assortment of areas within [[mass spectrometry]], ranging from fundamental research to instrument and method development to applications. Cooks' research interests over the course of his career have included the study of [[gas-phase ion chemistry]],{{R|C1}} [[tandem mass spectrometry]],{{R|C2}} angle-resolved mass spectrometry{{R|C3}} and energy-resolved mass spectrometry (ERMS);{{R|C4}} dissociation processes, including [[Collision-induced dissociation|collision-induced dissociation (CID)]],{{R|D1}} [[Surface-induced dissociation|surface-induced dissociation (SID)]],{{R|D2}} and [[Photodissociation|photodissociation (PD)]];{{R|D3}} and desorption processes, including [[Secondary ion mass spectrometry|secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS)]],{{R|E1}} laser desorption ionization (LDI){{R|E2}} and [[Desorption electrospray ionization|desorption electrospray ionization (DESI)]].{{R|E3}}

His research has ranged through areas from preparative mass spectrometry, ionization techniques and [[Quadrupole ion trap|quadrupole ion traps (QITs)]] and related technologies{{R|F1}} to as far afield as [[Abiogenesis|abiogenisis]] (also known as "the origin of life") via [[homochirality]].{{R|G1}}

== Awards and fellowships ==
* 1984 ACS Analytical Division's Chemical Instrumentation Award;
* 1985 Thomson Medal for International Service to Mass Spectrometry;
* 1990 and 1995 NSF Special Creativity Award;
* 1991 Frank H. Field & Joe Franklin Award, (ACS Award for Mass Spectrometry);
* 1997 Fisher Award (ACS Award for Analytical Chemistry);
* 2006 [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry|Distinguished Contribution in Mass Spectrometry Award]]{{R|pmid18160305}};
* 2008 [[Robert Boyle Prize for Analytical Science]];
* 2012 [[F. Albert Cotton#F.A. Cotton Medal for Excellence in Chemical Research|F.A. Cotton Medal for Excellence in Chemical Research]] of the [[American Chemical Society]];
* 2013 [[Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences]];
* 2014 ACS Nobel Laureate Signature Award for Graduate Education in Chemistry, shared with graduate student Livia S. Eberlin{{R|purdue}};
* 2015 Member, [[National Academy of Sciences]];
* 2017 [[Aston Medal]], [[British Mass Spectrometry Society]].
